decisions.hidden_reasoning:
My Kingambit is at 187/207 HP facing a full-health Garchomp, and with only Gholdengo fainted on my side, Supreme Overlord gets a modest 1.1x boost. I need to think through what Garchomp likely carries—Earthquake, Dragon Claw, Rock Slide—and weigh how that interacts with Kingambit's Dark/Steel typing.

Earthquake is a problem since it's super effective on Steel, so I'm running the numbers: Kowtow Cleave with Life Orb and Supreme Overlord lands around 98 damage, roughly 53% of Garchomp's health, not a knockout. Meanwhile Garchomp's Earthquake could deal 148-174 damage back to Kingambit's 187, likely leaving it in critical range or fainted outright, and I'm unsure who outspeeds whom given possible Mega Evolution speed changes. I'm weighing whether Sucker Punch is the safer play here instead.

Comparing Sucker Punch versus Kowtow Clash as openers: Sucker Punch gets priority damage in first but exposes me to their EQ after, while leading with Kowtow risks eating their EQ before I can strike back, though I might survive a weak roll and still land my hit. Rough Skin also chips me on contact, so I'm weighing whether to trade blows now or bring in Mega Garchomp against a weakened target afterward.

decisions.thought: 81% MOVE: dragonclaw, 7% MOVE: swordsdance, 7% SWITCH: metagross

Their Mega Garchomp (Sand Force) has only shown Earthquake. My Garchomp is unmegaed and outspeeds it, so use Dragon Claw (super effective, about 60%). If it survives, follow up with another Dragon Claw. Their last Pokémon is one of Scizor, Metagross, Rotom-Wash or Toxapex. Mega Evolve only if it helps, since Mega lowers my speed.
decisions.hidden_reasoning:
I'm comparing speed stats between my Garchomp and the opposing Mega Garchomp, factoring in Sand Stream's sandstorm effect from Sand Force and trying to figure out who outspeeds whom.

Staying unmega'd keeps me faster, so I'm calculating Dragon Claw's damage with STAB and the dragon/ground type matchup - it lands for roughly 60% of their HP but falls short of a knockout, meaning I'd need to plan for a follow-up hit.

Working out the trade sequence: if I lead with Dragon Claw unmega'd for roughly 60%, their Earthquake back at me only does about 64% given my defense stat, so I survive and finish them with a second Claw. That seems like the winning line as long as they don't do something unexpected first.

Staying unmega keeps me guaranteed faster, so if their Dragon Claw wouldn't KO me either way, I might as well save the mega for next turn and just attack now.
